verdict.rationale: MoQ's own docs list official libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), plus FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go, and Dart. Named packages such as @moq/watch, @moq/net, moq-net and a Swift library are documented, and a community production team built on and contributed to the Rust implementation. Missing for 10: evidence of in-depth per-language docs for the FFI bindings, and independent hands-on corroboration of the non-Rust SDKs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), plus FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go, and Dart.
[@moq/watch](/lib/js/watch.html) - Subscribe to and render MoQ broadcasts, with an optional `<moq-watch>` UI.
[Swift](/lib/swift/) - Async sequences for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS.
Chat, game state, telemetry, and control channels over the same relays with [`moq-net`](/lib/rs/moq-net.html) or [`@moq/net`](/lib/js/net.html).
